categories.main_business_segments: Akamai operates three core business segments: Security (web application and API protection, DDoS mitigation, zero trust solutions), Content Delivery (web/mobile performance, media delivery, video streaming), and Compute (cloud computing services including compute, storage, networking, database, and container management). The company also provides professional services and support across these offerings through its Akamai Connected Cloud platform.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Akamai's core technology is its massively distributed edge and cloud platform called Akamai Connected Cloud, comprising over 4,100 edge points-of-presence across approximately 130 countries and nearly 750 cities with roughly 1,200 network partners. The platform leverages intelligent performance optimization, real-time monitoring, behavioral analytics, microsegmentation, and distributed computing architecture to deliver security, content delivery, and compute services at scale with single-digit millisecond latency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Akamai serves global enterprises across multiple industries including media and entertainment, e-commerce, financial services, technology, telecommunications, and government. Key customers include Adobe, Airbnb, Alibaba, eBay, Electronic Arts, Epic Games, Spotify, Sony Interactive Entertainment, and major U.S. government agencies. The company serves billions of end users globally who work, learn, shop, bank, and communicate online.
categories.geographic_coverage: Akamai operates globally with presence in approximately 130 countries and nearly 750 cities. As of December 31, 2023, the company had over 10,250 employees located in more than 30 countries, with approximately 60% located outside the U.S. Major office locations include Cambridge Massachusetts (headquarters), Bangalore India, Krakow Poland, and Tel Aviv Israel. International operations represented 48.4% of revenue in 2023.
categories.supply_chain_position: Akamai operates at multiple points in the supply chain as a midstream and downstream provider. The company relies on upstream suppliers for bandwidth, co-location facilities, server equipment, and third-party cloud services. It delivers services directly to enterprise customers and through channel partners including resellers, system integrators, and technology solution distributors, positioning itself between infrastructure providers and end customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Akamai's strategic priorities focus on growing security and compute solutions as the fastest-growing areas of the business. Key R&D initiatives include expanding zero trust security capabilities, advancing API security through the Neosec acquisition, scaling cloud computing infrastructure with 24 core computing regions globally, migrating third-party cloud services to Akamai Connected Cloud, and developing compute-to-edge solutions for enterprise customers. The company is investing significantly in platform modernization and security enhancements.
categories.revenue_model: Akamai generates revenue primarily through service contracts with terms of one year or longer, providing a consistent recurring revenue base. Revenue comes from security solutions, content delivery services, cloud computing services, and professional services. The company also generates usage-based revenue from traffic served on its network and has implemented price increases for certain compute solutions. Revenue is supplemented by one-time events and custom solution sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Akamai competes with diverse competitors ranging from startups to large technology and telecommunications companies. In security, it competes with hardware and software security providers. In content delivery, it faces competition from alternative CDN providers and DIY solutions. In compute, it increasingly competes with large hyperscaler cloud providers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. The company differentiates through its global scale, distributed network architecture, integrated security and compute offerings, and unique edge-to-cloud platform.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Akamai is a large-cap technology company with 2023 revenue of $3.81 billion, representing 5.4% growth year-over-year. The company generated $1.35 billion in operating cash flow in 2023 and maintains a strong balance sheet with $2.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Net income was $548 million in 2023. The company shows moderate overall growth with strong growth in security (14.5%) and compute (24.4%) segments, offset by declining delivery revenue (-7.6%).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Akamai's primary value proposition is its massively distributed Akamai Connected Cloud platform that provides unmatched global scale, visibility into internet traffic patterns, and the ability to deliver security, performance, and compute services with single-digit millisecond latency. Key differentiators include the unique edge-to-cloud computing continuum, integrated security and delivery capabilities, global network visibility enabling threat detection, and the ability to help enterprises compete with scale and resilience while reducing infrastructure complexity and costs.
